about: Words that must not be in what the Coach model is given or told to say, because the app never shows them to a user in that sense.

This is the one list. proxy/test/worker.test.js holds the Coach instructions and the summary the Worker hands the model to it; ios/RepToday/RepTodayTests/CoachRequestVocabularyTests.swift holds the app's side to it.
'tier' is deliberately not here: the Progress tab shows 'Tier 2 of 4 - next tier in reach', so it is the app's own word.
forms: each form is a run of whole words, matched case-insensitively after splitting camelCase and punctuation, so 'chainPositions' matches 'chain' and 'discipline' does not match 'line'.
say: what the instructions tell the Coach to say instead. null means the word is only kept out of what the Coach is given, without naming it to the model.
onlyWith: the one sense the app does use the word in. A sentence of the instructions may use the word only if it also names this.
proof: where the app does or does not show the word.

words.say: 'foundation', or 'side' for the Squat side and the Hinge side of Legs
words.proof: The app never calls a foundation a line. Its only uses of the word are 'Your trend line grows as the weeks add up' (ProgressTabView) and 'One line, in your words' (OnboardingView).

words.say: 'next tier in reach' for a next tier or movement, keeping 'unlock' for what earning the Strength Phase opens
words.proof: Every use in the app is about what the Strength Phase or Premium opens: 'Earn the Strength Phase to unlock', 'Strength skill - unlocked', 'the full catalog is unlocked' (ProgressTabView), 'More movements unlock when you earn the Strength Phase' (ReadyView), and the Premium upsell. A next tier is 'next tier in reach' or 'Coming up', never locked.

words.say: that they are working toward the Strength Phase
words.proof: No string in the app contains 'discipline'; the app names only the Strength Phase. It reaches the Worker as the phase value 'discipline', which the Worker hands to the model as 'Strength Phase: not earned yet.'
